title: Balancing chemical equation
competency: Balance simple chemical equations by inspection and by the LCM method.

keywords.def: An equation with the same number of each kind of atom on both sides.
Balancing by trial: change coefficients until atoms are equal on both sides.
Balancing using the least common multiple of total valence numbers.

en.text: A balanced equation has the same number of each kind of atom on both sides. This obeys the law of conservation of mass. Change only the coefficients, never the subscripts. Inspection is trial and error: N₂ + H₂ → NH₃ becomes N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃.

screens.title: A tempting shortcut
screens.ask: To balance H₂ + O₂ → H₂O, Abebe changes it to H₂ + O₂ → H₂O₂. Is that allowed?
opts: No, he changed water into a new substance
screens.after:
Changing a subscript changes the substance.
H₂O is water. H₂O₂ is hydrogen peroxide, a different substance.
Only coefficients may change: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O.
screens.best: No, he changed water into a new substance

screens.title: 3.3.6 Balancing chemical equation
paras: A chemical equation is balanced to obey the law of conservation of mass.
In a balanced equation, the atoms on the left equal the atoms on the right.
We change the coefficients, not the subscripts.
Changing subscripts changes the identity of substances.

screens.title: Coefficient or subscript? Look at 2H₂O
items: The coefficient. It means two molecules of water. We may change it.
The subscript. Each water molecule has 2 H atoms. Never change it.
No subscript means 1 O atom in each molecule.

screens.title: Two methods
paras: This grade uses two methods: the inspection method and the LCM method.
Inspection is a trial and error method.
Adjust the coefficients until each kind of atom is equal on both sides.

screens.title: Inspection: making ammonia
steps: N: 2 on the left. Put 2 before NH₃: N₂ + H₂ → 2NH₃.
Now H: 2 × 3 = 6 on the right. Put 3 before H₂: N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃.

screens.title: Key words
defs: An equation with the same number of each kind of atom on both sides.
Balancing by trial: change coefficients until atoms are equal on both sides.

screens.text: Balancing rule: true or false? When we balance an equation, we change the subscripts but not the coefficients.
screens.why:
A subscript is part of the formula.
Changing H₂O to H₂O₂ makes a different substance.
So we change only the coefficients.
The statement is false.
screens.clue: What would changing H₂O to H₂O₂ do?

screens.text: Balance by inspection: H₂ + I₂ → HI
screens.why:
Count H: 2 on the left, 1 in HI.
Put 2 before HI: 2HI.
Now H: 2 = 2 and I: 2 = 2.
So H₂ + I₂ → 2HI.
H₂I₂ changes the subscripts, which is not allowed.

screens.title: Exercise 3.6 Q1 d
steps: O: left 1, right 2. Put 2 before H₂O.

screens.text: Balance by inspection: Ca + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + H₂
screens.why:
Ca: 1 on each side.
O: left 1, right 2 in Ca(OH)₂. Put 2 before H₂O.
H: left 2 × 2 = 4. Right 2 + 2 = 4.
So Ca + 2H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + H₂.

screens.text: Challenge, balance by inspection: Fe₂O₃ + CO → Fe + CO₂
screens.why:
Fe: 2 in Fe₂O₃, so put 2 before Fe.
Each CO becomes one CO₂, so they get the same coefficient x.
O: left 3 + x, right 2x. So 3 + x = 2x, and x = 3.
Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂.
Check: Fe 2 = 2, C 3 = 3, O 3 + 3 = 6 = 3 × 2.
screens.clue: Count O on both sides with the same number before CO and CO₂.

en.text: In the LCM method, find each total valence (subscript × valence), find the LCM of these numbers, then divide the LCM by each total to get the coefficients. For aluminum and oxygen: totals 3, 4 and 6 give LCM 12, so 4Al + 3O₂ → 2Al₂O₃.

screens.title: A common number
screens.ask: Al has total valence 3, O₂ has 4, Al₂O₃ has 6. What is the smallest number all three divide into?
screens.after:
12 ÷ 3 = 4, 12 ÷ 4 = 3 and 12 ÷ 6 = 2.
6 is not divisible by 4. 24 works, but it is not the smallest.
So 12 is the least common multiple (LCM). The LCM method uses it.

screens.title: Total valence = atoms × valence
screens.ask: Al + O₂ → Al₂O₃. Al has valence 3, O has valence 2. Tap each formula.

screens.title: The LCM method
steps: Step 1, word equation: aluminum + oxygen → aluminum oxide.
Step 3, total valences: Al = 1 × 3 = 3; O₂ = 2 × 2 = 4; Al₂O₃ = 2 × 3 = 6.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Balancing using the least common multiple of total valence numbers.

screens.text: LCM method: for Al + O₂ → Al₂O₃, find the LCM of the total valences 3, 4 and 6.
screens.why:
Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18 …
6 is not divisible by 4.
12 ÷ 3 = 4 and 12 ÷ 4 = 3.
So the LCM of 3, 4 and 6 is 12.
72 is a common multiple, but not the least.

screens.text: Balance by the LCM method: Fe + O₂ → Fe₂O₃ (Fe valence 3)
screens.why:
Total valences: Fe = 1 × 3 = 3; O₂ = 2 × 2 = 4; Fe₂O₃ = 2 × 3 = 6.
LCM of 3, 4 and 6 is 12.
Divide: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 (Fe); 12 ÷ 4 = 3 (O₂); 12 ÷ 6 = 2 (Fe₂O₃).
4Fe + 3O₂ → 2Fe₂O₃.
Check: Fe 4 = 4, O 6 = 6.

screens.ask: Count the atoms: in 4Al + 3O₂ → 2Al₂O₃ there are ___ oxygen atoms on each side.
screens.why:
Atoms = coefficient × subscript.
Left: 3O₂ gives 3 × 2 = 6 oxygen atoms.
Right: 2Al₂O₃ gives 2 × 3 = 6 oxygen atoms.
So there are 6 on each side.

screens.text: Challenge, balance: Cu + H₂SO₄ → CuSO₄ + SO₂ + H₂O
screens.why:
Cu: 1 on each side.
S: right has CuSO₄ and SO₂, so 2 S. Put 2 before H₂SO₄.
H: left 2 × 2 = 4. Put 2 before H₂O.
O: left 2 × 4 = 8; right 4 + 2 + 2 = 8.
So Cu + 2H₂SO₄ → CuSO₄ + SO₂ + 2H₂O.
screens.clue: Balance S first, then H, then check O.

items.text: Balance by inspection: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂
items.why:
Count each atom.
Ca: 1 = 1. C: 1 = 1.
O: left 3; right 1 + 2 = 3.
All are equal, so it is already balanced.

items.text: Balance by inspection: H₂ + I₂ → HI
items.why:
H: 2 on the left, 1 in HI. Put 2 before HI.
Then H: 2 = 2 and I: 2 = 2.
So H₂ + I₂ → 2HI.

items.text: Balance by inspection: C₂H₂ + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O
items.why:
C: 2 in C₂H₂, so 2CO₂.
H: 2 in C₂H₂, so 1 H₂O.
O: right 2 × 2 + 1 = 5, so 5/2 O₂. A half is not allowed.
Double everything: 2C₂H₂ + 5O₂ → 4CO₂ + 2H₂O.
Check: C 4 = 4, H 4 = 4, O 10 = 8 + 2.

items.text: Balance by inspection: Ca + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + H₂
items.why:
Ca: 1 = 1.
O: right has 2 in Ca(OH)₂. Put 2 before H₂O.
H: left 4; right 2 + 2 = 4.
So Ca + 2H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + H₂.

items.text: Balance by inspection: Fe₂O₃ + CO → Fe + CO₂
items.why:
Fe: put 2 before Fe.
CO and CO₂ need the same coefficient: try 3.
O: left 3 + 3 = 6; right 3 × 2 = 6.
So Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂.
Check: Fe 2 = 2, C 3 = 3, O 6 = 6.
items.clue: Same number before CO and CO₂.

items.text: Balance by the LCM method: Fe + O₂ → Fe₂O₃
items.why:
Total valences: Fe 1 × 3 = 3; O₂ 2 × 2 = 4; Fe₂O₃ 2 × 3 = 6.
LCM of 3, 4 and 6 = 12.
Coefficients: 12 ÷ 3 = 4, 12 ÷ 4 = 3, 12 ÷ 6 = 2.
4Fe + 3O₂ → 2Fe₂O₃. Check: Fe 4 = 4, O 6 = 6.

items.text: Balance: Cu + H₂SO₄ → CuSO₄ + SO₂ + H₂O
items.why:
S: 2 on the right (CuSO₄ and SO₂). Put 2 before H₂SO₄.
H: 4 on the left. Put 2 before H₂O.
O: left 8; right 4 + 2 + 2 = 8.
Cu: 1 = 1. Balanced.

test.text: True or false: a balanced equation has equal numbers of each kind of atom on both sides.
test.why:
Balanced means the atoms are conserved.
Each kind of atom has the same number on both sides.
So the statement is true.

test.text: Balancing rule: to balance an equation we change the
test.why:
Subscripts are part of each formula.
Changing them changes the substance.
So we change only the coefficients.
Symbols name the elements and never change.

test.text: Balance by inspection: N₂ + H₂ → NH₃
test.why:
N: 2 on the left. Put 2 before NH₃.
H: right 2 × 3 = 6. Put 3 before H₂.
N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃.
Check: N 2 = 2, H 6 = 6.

test.text: Balance by inspection: Mg + O₂ → MgO
test.why:
O: 2 on the left, 1 in MgO. Put 2 before MgO.
Mg: now 2 on the right. Put 2 before Mg.
2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO.
Check: Mg 2 = 2, O 2 = 2.
MgO₂ changes a subscript, which is not allowed.

test.text: Balance by inspection: Al(OH)₃ → Al₂O₃ + H₂O
test.why:
Al: 2 in Al₂O₃. Put 2 before Al(OH)₃.
H: left 2 × 3 = 6. Put 3 before H₂O.
O: left 2 × 3 = 6; right 3 + 3 = 6.
So 2Al(OH)₃ → Al₂O₃ + 3H₂O.

notes.text: Balancing is asked as multiple choice (typing coefficients and subscripts is hard on a phone); every option is checked by counting atoms.
